extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners in bacteriology / laboratory technicians
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory procedures and equipment-selection standards for bacteriological work, including sterilisation by filtration, setup and use of porcelain filter systems and pumps, and detailed specifications for microscopes and micrometry methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotton-wool air filter method for sterilising gases
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise gases before admission to a vessel by passing them through a bulb of dry cotton-wool within glass tubing; connect via sterile rubber tubing to the culture flask inlet so gas passes through dry sterile cotton-wool and enters in a sterile condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct filter from glass tubing with a blown bulb filled with dry cotton-wool, wrap cotton at each end and sterilise in hot-air oven. Sterilise rubber tubing by boiling, transfer through absolute alcohol, burn off alcohol in flame before connecting. Rapidly couple sterile pieces to avoid contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Porcelain (and Kieselguhr) filter use for sterilising liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise liquids by passing them through cylindrical porous porcelain (Chamberland) or Kieselguhr (Berkefeld) 'filter candles' which retain bacteria in their pores while allowing liquid to pass germ-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select candles without metal fittings (avoid cracks from unequal expansion). Pores must be extremely minute; Chamberland candles have finer channels (slower filtration). To hasten filtration use aspiration, pressure, or both. Doultons white porcelain noted as efficient and faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus required for porcelain filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential items for filtration: separatory funnel, sterile filter candle fitted with perforated rubber stopper and rubber washer, sterile filter flask with cotton-wool plug, suction or pressure pump (Sprengel, Geryk), air filter sterilised, pressure tubing, screw clamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an air pump with oil seals (Geryk), interpose a Wulff's bottle with sulphuric acid between filter flask and pump to prevent moist air reaching pump oil. Ensure all fittings sterile and appropriate for vacuum/pressure used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration by aspiration: procedural steps and sterile handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When filtering by suction, couple exhaust to lateral tube, remove cotton plug and fit candle, attach separatory funnel, exhaust air, maintain vacuum until complete, then close and relieve vacuum carefully before disconnecting and sterilising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After filtration: close funnel tap, apply screw clamp to lateral branch, disconnect acid wash-bottle, attach air filter and allow filtered air to abolish negative pressure gradually, detach tubing and flame ends, plug orifices with sterile cotton-wool, remove filter candle and flame mouth, boil filter candle and separatory funnel for disinfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pressure (Pakes' reservoir) for rapid filtration and sterilisation
rubrics_metrics.description: For rapid filtration of large bulk fluids use pressure in conjunction with vacuum, employing a pressure-resistant metal receptacle (Pakes' reservoir) fitted to hold the filter candle and fluid and maintain positive pressure (about 1–1.5 atmospheres) while vacuum is kept on the receiving flask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sterilise Pakes' reservoir by assembling candle, wrapping delivery tube with cotton-wool, plugging neck, and autoclaving at 120°C for twenty minutes. After cooling, screw together, connect compressed gas cylinder and exhaust pump, raise pressure to desired reading (usually 1–1.5 atm), and maintain until filtration completes. Ensure nuts and fittings are sterilised (immerse in boiling water before screwing on).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterilisation of rubber and pressure tubing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise short lengths of rubber tubing by boiling, transfer through absolute alcohol, and pass through flame to burn off alcohol immediately before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle tubing with sterile forceps, drain thoroughly after alcohol, and flame to remove last traces. Rapidly couple to sterile glassware to avoid contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid metal fittings on filter candles
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting porcelain filter candles avoid those with metal fittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metal fittings develop cracks at junctions with siliceous material during sterilisation due to unequal expansion; choose all-siliceous fittings where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Wulff's bottle with sulphuric acid to protect vacuum pumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpose a Wulff's bottle, fitted as a wash-bottle containing sulphuric acid, between filter flask and exhaust pump when using oil-sealed pumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents moist air from reaching low-vapour-tension oil in the pump, protecting its seal and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscope: general physical and optical essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscope for bacteriological work should be monocular, of good workmanship, rigid, firm, free from vibration, with smooth precise joints and movements, conforming to the Royal Microscopical Society's standard, fitted with good lenses and a sufficiently large stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid instruments with 'loss of time' or 'slipping' defects; ensure stability in all positions including inclined and horizontal. Emphasises build quality and optical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base/foot standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Base or foot should provide stability and ease of manipulation; tripod or horse-shoe forms are common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tripod is mechanically preferred and often shod with cork for stability; the Jackson foot is an alternative with good appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body tube length compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Body tube may be 'long/English' (250 mm.) or 'short/Continental' (160 mm.); objectives must be manufactured for the chosen tube length or the instrument should provide a draw tube to accommodate different objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In high-class microscopes a shorter tube with draw tube allows use of either form of objective; for practical purposes the tube length equals distance from nosepiece end to eyeglass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coarse adjustment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Coarse adjustment should be rack-and-pinion, with steadiness and smoothness ensured by dovetailed bearings and accurate correspondence between rack teeth and pinion leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision should be made for taking up 'slack' (e.g., by adjustable screws) to maintain smooth action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine adjustment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine adjustment must not rely on direct action of springs but be of the lever pattern (preferably Nelson), giving very delicate movement and reducing load on the vertical screw thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lever pattern uses unequal arm lengths for sensitivity; a spindle milled head accessory is useful for rapid medium-power adjustments and fine focusing at high powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage should be square, at least 12 cm in area, flat and rigid to support Petri dishes and slides; supply spring clips and preferably an integral mechanical stage with stationary milled heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical stage is necessary for high-power and hanging-drop work; prefer one forming an integral part of the instrument and tapped for removable screw studs to accept Vernier or Maltwood finders; aperture shape should be square to allow free movement of substage condenser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diaphragm preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid separate single diaphragms; prefer a revolving plate with different apertures or, best, an iris diaphragm incorporated into the substage condenser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iris diaphragms give variable aperture control and integrate with condensers for better illumination control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substage condenser requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A substage condenser (Abbe type generally) is necessary to collect and focus light into a cone of large, adjustable aperture; it must be accurately centered with the objective and focussable for object plane thickness variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical rack-and-pinion movement is advantageous; condenser should be removable from optical axis if needed. For oil-immersion objectives an achromatic condenser giving a cone about 0.9 is recommended; good centering and accurate focussing are essential to realise condenser benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mirrors usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A reversible circular frame carrying a plane mirror on one side and concave on the other is typical; plane mirror usually used, concave useful for low powers when condenser is racked down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide gimbal mounting so mirror can be oriented as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ocular (eyepiece) selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Huyghenian oculars are sufficient for ordinary work; two or three giving 4x, 6x, 8x magnification are useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ehrlich's eyepiece (adjustable square diaphragm) is helpful for enumeration tasks. Some special eyepieces include sledging adjustments for micrometer focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives: required types and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Three objectives are necessary (low-power e.g., 1", 2/3", 1/2"; medium e.g., 1/6" or 1/8" dry; high-power e.g., 1/12" oil immersion). Selection must pay attention to: (a) correction of spherical aberration, (b) correction of chromatic aberration, (c) flatness of field, (d) good definition, (e) numerical aperture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual magnification is less important than clear definition and resolving power. Flatness of field means peripheral and central zones can be focused with fine adjustment — indicates perfect lens centering. Numerical aperture determines brightness, resolving and defining powers; good objectives are typically achromatic and avoid need for costly apochromats for routine work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective testing objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Best test objects for selecting objectives are: (1) thin one-cell-layer 'blood film' stained with Jenner's or Romanowsky's stain and (2) thin cover-slip preparation of young cultivation of B. diphtheriae stained with methylene-blue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these preparations to assess objective performance at appropriate nominal focal lengths (listed per lens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessories: nosepiece and centering
rubrics_metrics.description: Nosepiece to carry two or three objectives (preferably covered-in type of aluminium) is useful; for critical work and photo-micrography a special sliding carrier nosepiece (Zeiss/Leitz) ensures accurate centering of each objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interchangeable nosepieces may be imperfect for critical work due to centering inaccuracies; use precision carriers when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warm stage and temperature control
rubrics_metrics.description: Warm stage (metal case with circulating water) clamps onto the stage to permit raising temperature of preparations for observations (spore germination, hanging-drop cultures). Electrical hot stages (Lorrain Smith design) provide precise temperature control using electric coils and rheostat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electrical hot stage requires lamp resistance, sliding rheostat, and delicate ammeter; immersion oil contact between condenser top lens and bulb lower surface improves performance with 1/12-inch oil immersion lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark-ground (paraboloid) condenser usage and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Dark-ground condenser is an immersion substage condenser of high aperture to show unstained objects as bright on a dark background; central rays are blocked while peripheral rays are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires powerful illuminant (arc or incandescent gas lamp), picked slides of specified thickness (generally ~1 mm), very thin cover-glasses (≤0.17 mm), and objectives with NA ≤ 1.0 (immersion lenses must have internal stop to cut down aperture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrometry: need for stage micrometer
rubrics_metrics.description: All micrometry methods require a stage micrometer (3x1 inch slip engraved to hundredths of a millimetre) as the standard for calibrating eyepiece, filar, or camera-lucida measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover-glass protects the scale; calibrate each optical combination and record values carefully for repeatable measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrometry by camera lucida
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach camera lucida to eyepiece, project stage micrometer scale onto paper, sketch magnified image marking that optical combination; repeat for each ocular-objective-tube combination to preserve scales for measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark optical combination used with each scale. Alternatively project object and micrometer scale on same paper ensuring consistent eye-to-paper distance (25 cm) for subsequent measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrometry by eyepiece micrometer and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Eyepiece micrometer (glass disc with scale) must be focused in the eyepiece; its division value must be ascertained for each optical combination by comparing with stage micrometer and using the relation given (x = 10 y in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make lines parallel by rotating ocular, make two lines of eyepiece coincide with stage micrometer division, note included divisions and calculate value in micra; record optical combination and micrometer values for later measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wright's Eikonometer usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Eikonometer is a modification of eyepiece micrometer for rapid measurement by direct inspection after determining magnifying power constants for each optical combination using a stage micrometer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine magnifying constant by aligning eikonometer scale with stage micrometer (e.g., five stage divisions filling one eikonometer division indicates magnification constant 500). Record constants and thereafter divide observed size by constant to obtain actual size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrometry by filar (Ramsden's) micrometer and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Filar micrometer eyepiece has fixed and movable wires moved by a micrometer screw; value of micrometer comb divisions must be determined for each optical combination by using the stage micrometer and recording revolutions and drum fractions needed to traverse known distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set movable wire to coincide with fixed, zero drum head, focus both scales, make lines parallel, move to traverse a known 0.01 mm and note revolutions and fractions; average several estimations and record values per optical combination for later measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscope illuminant recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use diffuse daylight in tropical/subtropical regions; in temperate regions electricity is best (obscured metal filament lamp ~16 candle power recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If monochromatic light is needed, streak blue grease pencil over lamp ground glass and heat to distribute film evenly. For lamps use weighted base and a reflector; gas or incandescent mantles are alternatives if electricity unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential apparatus and reagents for routine microscopical examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be provided with: india-rubber change-mat for cover-glasses, blotting paper squares (~10 cm), a glass jar with 2% lysol for infected cover-glasses/pipettes, glazed earthenware disinfectant box with removable lining of 2% lysol, Bunsen burner with peep-flame, porcelain trough for hanging-drop slides, and properly prepared hanging-drop slides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'German lined' filter paper for blotting (highly absorbent, no loose fluff). Hanging-drop slides: Boettcher's ring slide modification preferred; avoid ground concavity slides which are more easily contaminated. Keep disinfectant receptacles and procedures for handling infected material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and preparation of platinum-iridium loops (inoculating wires)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aluminium rods carrying platino-iridium wire loops (one with an oval loop called 'oese') are essential for transfers and manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications: rods approx. 25 cm long carrying 0.015 gauge platino-iridium wire 7.5 cm in length; loop dimensions and wire mounting as described for routine bacteriological manipulations.
